RECORD OF INVESTIGATION.

On the 5-12-33 a report was received at Louza station from D.S.Tilton(Special Branch) stating that as a result of enquiries made by Supt.Tan Shao Liang (S.M.P.) the S.P.S.B.on the statements of their Honorary Detective Woo Zih Ching(吴泽卿)(person who caused the man to be arrested)claim that the arrested man is the Secretary of the Provincial Committee of the Chinese Communist Youth League.

Detective Woo also stated that at the time of his recognising the man on the 30-11-33, the man was with two other communists named Ning Gee Ziang (任其祥) and Tsaung Goh Ming (章耀明).

The arrested man was questioned by D.S.Elders and C.D.S.211 on the 5-12-33 re these two men but he denied knowing any such men and stated he was alone when he was arrested.

On the 5-12-33 a.m. the five persons in custody in connection with the murder of Wong Yoong Hwa and others were questioned by D.Ss.Logan, Elders and C.D.S.211 re the two names given but they also denied knowing them or the arrested man.

The arrested man will again appear before the High Court on the 6-12-33 when the S.P.S.B.intend to press for his extradition.

Made by D.S. Tilton Forwarded by [签名]

Inquiries made through Supt. Tan Shao Liang, Municipal
Police Headquarters, reveal that the accused Ling Ts Ching is
the Secretary of the Provincial Committee of the Chinese Communist
Youth League. This information is furnished by Honorary Detective
Woo Zuh Ching (吴泽卿), Shanghai Public Safety Bureau, a converted
communist and former assistant working under the late Wong Yoong
Hwa (黄永华), Nanking Political Agent. Detective Woo is regarded
as a very reliable man and states that when first observing the
accused Ling Ts Ching (林子清) alias Tseu Lien Woo (周廉武) on
November 30 he intended to shadow him, but the accused was later
joined by other male Chinese communists among whom were two named
Ning Gee Ziang (任其祥) and Tsaung Yoh Ming (章耀明). The latter
are both known to Detective Woo but unfortunately they recognised
him at this chance meeting with the result as already contained in
earlier reports. It is believed by the Shanghai Public Safety
Bureau that the party of communists had designs to kidnap
Detectives Woo and Wong or take some revenge upon them, but the
chance meeting gave them no time to form a definite plan or carry
it out and the subsequent action of the detectives in giving the
alarm frustrated their intentions.

In connection with these two male communists who both made
their escape named Ning Gee Ziang (任其祥) and Tsaung Yoh Ming
(章耀明), the latter is definitely reported by the Shanghai Public
Safety Bureau to be a member of the Special Administration Bureau
of the Chinese Communist Party, while the other is likewise believed
to be a member.

The arrested man Ling Ts Ching (林子清) appeared before the High Court on the 1-12-33 and was ordered remanded in custody for further enquiries until the 6-12-33. He has no previous convictions. The S.P.S.B. Detective Woo who caused the man to be arrested, appeared and gave evidence in Court.

With regard to the six papers found in the accused's possession, he stated that these are not his property and must have been put in his pocket by the detectives. C.D.S.211(Louza) states he personally took these papers from the accused's pocket at the station. Five of the six papers are receipts for various items purchased from different shops therefore, between 10.35 a.m. and 12.20 p.m.2-12-33, D.S. Elders and C.D.S.211 took the accused to the shops in question and ascertained the following:-

Receipt No.1 refers to a small 'Anchor' spirit stove purchased at the Sun Sun Company, Nanking Road on the 31-10-33 for $3.75.

Receipt No.2,3 and 4 refer to a quantity of plain white paper wrapping paper purchased at the San Yih Sing(三益新) Paper shop, 312 Sinza Road on the 27-11-33, 15-11-33 and 4-11-33 for $1.20, $3.00 and $3.00.

Receipt No.5 refers to the same kind of paper purchased from the Tuck Tai Foong Paper Company (德泰丰), 502 Canton Road on the 3-11-33 for $3.10.

Ling Ts Ching (林子清) age 28, Changhwa.

Louza Stn. 2-12-33. ---------- Y.P.Sih.

I am a resident of Kwang-tuh Hsien, Anhwei. In March, 1928,
I arrived in Shanghai and was employed at the Ting Sing (鼎新)
Wine shop at the corner of Burkill and Myburgh Roads, as an
assistant. From March to April, 1929, I then became a teacher
at the Kwen-chun (艺军) School, Rue Cassini, French Concession.
Later, I managed the Dong Ding Poo (洞庭波) Wine shop, No.200
Rue Brenier Montmorend, French Concession and purchased the
said shop as my own to carry on business in January 1930.
In May that year, I sub-let the upstairs front room of the
premises to one Woo (吴) who removed away after having
occupied the room for over two months. Later, detectives
visited there and made enquiries with a view of locating
Woo. In February 1931, owing to lack of capital I disposed
of the above wine shop to two men namely Tsang (张) and
Wong (王), obtaining $300.00. From that time onward, I
resided at an upstairs room of Ssu Kyl (四吉) Wine shop,
1004 Jukieng Road, Chapei and earned my livelihood by teaching
two small boys primary Chinese readers. I returned to my
home at Anhwei when the Shanghai War took place on 28-1-32.
With the intention of seeking employment at Shanghai, I,
on 29-11-33, left Anhwei for Li Yang thence to Changchow by
boat, and from there, on 30th, I took the morning train and
arrived in Shanghai at about 1 p.m. same date. At 2.30 p.m.
I went to buy a pair of socks at the Sincere Co., when I met
my former tenant Woo. He accosted me and asked me to follow
him to Nanking Road, where I was surrounded by three or four
persons who were called by Woo. Being afraid, I ran to
Kiukiang and Yunnan Roads and then South to Canton Road but
was followed and as two of them attempted to assault me,
I shouted for help. While I was running on Foochow Road near
Chekiang Road, I was arrested by Police.
Signed by accused.
